title: Retail and institutional investors are diverging in their appetite for AI stocks
key_facts: Business Insider, 16 Oct: Citadel Securities data show retail investors net bought $9.1 billion of US equities on its platform last week, the most in 15 weeks.
Chip stocks drew $2.6 billion of net inflows; the $700 million into neocloud stocks was the largest weekly retail buying in that group the firm has seen.
Weekly retail net buying rose from $4.8 billion to $6.4 billion to $9.1 billion over three weeks.
Viraj Patel, global market strategist at Vanda Research, flagged a 'buyer's strike' by institutions and said institutional investors are rotating from growth and quality to defensive shares.
Patel said retail bought a record amount of CoreWeave on Thursday despite the sell-off, while institutional options flows in AI baskets deteriorated.
Patel also said retail dip-buying has been less consistent in 2026 and asked whether it is enough to offset the fading institutional bid.
quote_evidence: Last week, retail net bought $9.1 billion of US equities on our platform, the largest weekly net buying in 15 weeks (since late June) and the ninth-largest week over the past year.
The $700 million poured into neocloud stocks is the largest weekly buying spree the firm has observed among retail.
The institutional dip-buying appetite is clearly fading.
why_it_matters_hint: Small investors are buying the dip in AI stocks while big institutions are stepping back.
event_date: Week to 9 Oct and 15 Oct 2026; published 16 Oct
notes: Citadel data quoted from a note by Scott Rubner of Citadel Securities; his title is not given in the article, so he is not named in the entry.
